name: task-log
title: task-log
desc: Claude logs every task it completes to .claude/tasks.json — so you see at a glance what was done in a project, without asking.
pain: You cannot say what was done last week without asking

name: product-docs-spec
title: product-docs-spec
desc: Turns raw input — a client's description, specs, a CSV, a design export, existing code — into a docs/ folder of 12 files that works as the actual build spec: data model with types, roles matrix, every screen, processes, API, invariants, and open questions with defaults. Written before any code, so the product gets built right the first time.
prepend: Build the docs/ specification for THIS project by following the specification below in full. Read every input available first — the client's description, any .md/.docx/.pdf specs, datasets, design or code exports, the existing repository — and ground every statement in them; never invent. Write only inside docs/ in this pass: no application code yet.
pain: A client's description is not something you can build from

name: task-planner
title: task-planner
desc: Turns a goal into small, self-contained task files in tasks/todo/ — each carrying the right model context AND the step-by-step checks that prove it works, so nothing is called done on faith.
pain: Work arrives with no way to check it is done

name: task-runner
title: task-runner
desc: Works the whole task queue to empty, autonomously: todo → in progress → verify → done. It runs each task's checks for real, and when one fails it writes the fix task itself. Batch work without babysitting — and without silent breakage.
pain: The queue only moves while somebody pushes it

name: app-audit
title: app-audit
desc: Walks a running app end to end — every page, every interactive element, every route — works out what a user can actually accomplish, then proves each use case by executing it. Failures become fix tasks with the exact repro. It refuses to touch production and never presses a destructive control on data that matters.
pain: Nobody can say what actually works in the running app

name: spec-audit
title: spec-audit
desc: Reads the product's written rules against the code that implements them and records every disagreement on the objects it sits on — so it marks the diagrams and warns anyone planning a change, instead of scrolling out of a chat.
pain: You find out at the demo that the product does not do what you promised

name: legacy-maintenance
title: legacy-maintenance
desc: Change or maintain an existing legacy codebase without breaking the behaviour next to it — maps the blast radius from the model, then ships small reversible steps you can verify. For keeping old projects alive, not rewriting them.
pain: Changing old code breaks the thing standing next to it

name: stack-port
title: stack-port
desc: Port an old, hand-written project onto a new stack with full feature parity — the old app is the spec, a parity ledger keeps anything from being silently dropped, and every slice is verified against the old behaviour, not just a green build.
pain: A rewrite quietly loses features nobody wrote down
